# Event contract

`ms-go-learning-planner` publishes terminal planning outcomes through a
PostgreSQL transactional outbox to the infra-owned
`LEARNING_PLANNER_EVENTS` JetStream stream.

- `course.plan.completed`, schema versions 1 and 2; new writes use version 2;
- `course.plan.failed`, schema versions 1 and 2; new writes use version 2.
- `planner.onboarding-path.outcome.v1`, schema version 1.

S9 publishes that subject only for `PATH_READY`, `ACTIVE_PATH_EXISTS`, and
`STATE_CHANGED`. Internal executor failures are durable Planner evidence but
are not public S9 outcomes and create no outbox row.

The envelope contains `event_id`, `event_type`, `correlation_id` (planning
request UUID), `causation_id` (request idempotency UUID), `student_id`,
`occurred_at`, `schema_version`, and bounded `data`. Data contains request/goal
identity, terminal status, optional Course/result/failure codes, source,
reason, and audit references. Version 2 adds optional `learning_path_id`; it is
omitted for an unallocated new-path `NO_GAP`. It excludes prompt variables, generated content,
mastery detail, raw evidence, provider output, and reasoning.
The exact Student command checkpoint and its hash remain private request-row
audit data and are never copied into the envelope. A delivered Student `409`
after checkpointing produces `course.plan.failed` with
`failure_code=LEARNING_PATH_COMMAND_CONFLICT`.

Publication is at least once. `event_id` is deterministic per request and
terminal subject and is also the JetStream deduplication key. Consumers must
maintain a durable inbox and must accept version 2 before this producer is
deployed. Existing version-1 outbox rows remain valid and publishable.
`ms-go-teacher-agent` accepts only `source=TEACHER`
outcomes into its inbox and appends a notification only when a valid
general-Dialog audit reference exists; Student and system outcomes are
acknowledged without Teacher state or delivery.
